nodes.name: Birth Certificate
nodes.description: Registering a child's birth for Indian citizenship when born to Indian parents abroad, or attesting a birth certificate issued by Indian authorities.

sources.evidence: In order to get Indian citizenship for a child born to Indian parent(s) in a foreign country, the birth of the child is to be registered at the nearest Indian Embassy/Consulate and thereafter (or at the same time) the parents can apply for issue of an Indian passport for the child.

Yes, provided the birth certificate issued by the competent authorities has been authenticated by the Home Department of the concerned State/Union Territory in India and then by the Attestation Section of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), New Delhi or the MEA Branch Secretariats in Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Guwahati.

In order to get Indian citizenship for a child born to Indian parent(s) in a foreign country, the birth of the child is to be registered at the nearest Indian Embassy/Consulate and thereafter (or at the same time) the parents can apply for issue of an Indian passport for the child.

edges.note: The Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation can be contacted via a toll-free number for Birth & Death Certificate services.
The Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation's office address is Pandit Dindayal Upadhyay Bhavan, Behind Fire Station, Sector-17, Gandhinagar-382016.
